opportunity.title: FEMA's Deployment Management Solution (Sources Sought)
opportunity.description: FEMA is conducting market research for commercial off-the-shelf, configurable COTS, custom or hybrid solutions to replace the legacy Deployment Tracking System and improve incident workforce management: readiness, personnel availability, qualifications, certifications, training, deployment tracking, incident and event staffing, force packages, equipment assignment, reporting and analytics, secure cloud hosting, and interoperability with FEMA and DHS systems. Estimated value is $50 million to $100 million over five to ten years. Questions were due Oct 5, 2026.

rationale.point: Company is a large business with NAICS 541511 matching the opportunity, and the set-aside is NONE, so eligibility gate passed.

FEMA seeks a potential $100M replacement for its Deployment Tracking System, which aligns with Atlas Federal's past performance of prime IT contracts up to $60M including a Defense Health Agency data program.

Incumbent Intuitive Information Systems Technologies holds a $58.3M contract through 2027, but the Sources Sought indicates FEMA is planning a follow-on competition where Atlas can compete as a large business.

Atlas Federal holds a Top Secret facility clearance, FedRAMP Moderate authorization, and 150 cleared staff, supporting the security and compliance requirements likely needed for FEMA's incident workforce management system.

risks: Incumbent has an existing contract running until 2027, which may delay or shape the replacement acquisition.
Sources Sought is only a market research step, not a solicitation; no guarantee of a follow-on RFP or award.
Potential $100M value exceeds Atlas Federal's typical prime contract ceiling of $60M, possibly requiring teaming or growth.
Large business competition will be intense for a high-value, unrestricted opportunity.
nextSteps: Submit a capabilities response to the Sources Sought (solicitation 70FA3126I00000008) highlighting relevant past performance, clearances, FedRAMP status, and staffing.
Monitor for RFP release and engage in any industry days or draft RFP comment periods.
Evaluate teaming arrangements to strengthen capacity for a potential $100M+ program.
Leverage Defense Health Agency data program experience as a direct analog for FEMA's deployment management needs.
